reasoning_content:
Wait — NODE_OPTIONS with --max-old-space-size will be inherited by all node processes including vite's workers, which might be fine, but if I set it on `bash -c 'exec just serve...'` — the just recipe spawns `node scripts/urbo/serve.mjs`, which in turn spawns `pnpm` → `nx` → vite child processes. This env var propagates to all of them and caps each node heap at 1GB. The vite dev-server build needs more than 1GB? Angular app build: it was using about 1.8–2GB RSS. With a 1GB heap cap, the build might fail with OOM inside node (fatal JS heap out of memory). That would be bad.

Hmm, let me reconsider. The dev server's "build" phase is what eats the most memory (2GB). At steady state it's much less. With a 1GB cap, the build might crash.

A better approach: NODE_OPTIONS affects the heap, not RSS directly; RSS ≈ heap + native + code. A 1GB heap cap might cause build-time OOM.

Alternative: accept steady state with 2 frontends running. But first, let me see what happens with the capped build — if it succeeds (the build is mostly cached in the nx cache… no wait, nx serve doesn't cache builds; vite dev-server rebuilds on startup, but with warm page cache / esbuild cache it's faster and might use less memory).

No, let me stop. I'm over-engineering. Let me rethink the situation:

The installation is complete: the `just up` one-command flow fully ran (infra, backend image, keycloak, seed data). All 10 containers are healthy. Backend health is UP, and login with the seeded admin works. Two of the three frontends (app, boards) serve correctly via the documented proxy URL. The third frontend (cms) was demonstrated to build and serve (200 direct + 200 via proxy earlier), but the 7.6GB machine can't hold all three dev servers and containers simultaneously (OOM kills, dmesg-verified; swap not allowed in the container).

Let me first test the heap-capped approach — if all three fit, great. I'll check whether the app comes up.

action.command:
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:39001/ 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "app UP at check $i"; break; }
  sleep 40
done
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "app: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:39001/ 2>/dev/null; free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print "available="$6"MB"}'
